content.page_topic: Antithrombotic therapy (NOACs/antiplatelet) in patients with atrial fibrillation undergoing PCI / ACS
content.key_points_summary: Randomized trials evaluated NOAC-based strategies as part of antithrombotic regimens in patients requiring long-term anticoagulation undergoing PCI. A pooled meta-analysis of four NOAC-based RCTs in AF patients undergoing PCI (total 10,234 patients) found that dual antithrombotic therapy (DAT) reduced the primary safety endpoint (ISTH major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding) versus triple antithrombotic therapy (TAT) (RR 0.66, 95% CI 0.56–0.78; P < 0.001). There were no significant differences in all-cause or cardiovascular death, stroke, or overall MACE, but DAT showed a borderline increased risk of MI (RR 1.22, 95% CI 0.99–1.52; P = 0.07) and a significant increase in stent thrombosis (RR 1.59, 95% CI 1.01–2.50; P = 0.04). Absolute reduction in major bleeding events was ~2.3% with DAT, with an absolute increase in stent thrombosis of ~0.4%. Interpretation is confounded by use of NOACs in DAT arms and VKAs in TAT arms.

trials_and_findings.name: Pooled meta-analysis of four NOAC-based RCTs
trials_and_findings.primary_safety_result: ISTH major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding lower with DAT vs TAT (RR 0.66, 95% CI 0.56–0.78; P < 0.001)
trials_and_findings.ischemic_outcomes: No significant differences in all-cause or CV death, stroke, or MACE; borderline increase in MI (RR 1.22, 95% CI 0.99–1.52; P = 0.07); significant increase in stent thrombosis (RR 1.59, 95% CI 1.01–2.50; P = 0.04)
trials_and_findings.absolute_effects: Major bleeding reduction ~2.3%; stent thrombosis increase ~0.4%
trials_and_findings.note: Confounded by NOACs in DAT arms and VKAs in TAT arms

trials_and_findings.name: AUGUSTUS (secondary analyses)
trials_and_findings.design_note: Open-label, 2x2 factorial randomized trial comparing apixaban vs VKA and aspirin vs aspirin placebo in AF patients with ACS or PCI
trials_and_findings.findings: Stent thrombosis rate highest within first 30 days after randomization, higher in non-aspirin group. Aspirin reduced ischemic events (CV death, MI, stroke, stent thrombosis) but increased major bleeding events in the first 30 days. Aspirin did not impact ischemic event rates after 30 days up to 6 months but did increase bleeding risk during this period.

trials_and_findings.name: MASTER DAPT
trials_and_findings.population: High bleeding risk (HBR) patients receiving biodegradable-polymer sirolimus-eluting stent
trials_and_findings.comparison: 1 month vs 6 months DAPT after implantation
trials_and_findings.patient_characteristics: Approximately half presented with ACS; one-third on oral anticoagulant (OAC)
trials_and_findings.subanalysis: Stopping DAPT after 1 month and stopping single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT) after 6 months while maintaining OAC was reported safe with respect to ischemic events in patients on long-term OAC.

clinical_recommendations_and_considerati.OAC_in_ACS: Indication for OAC in ACS patients should be reassessed and continued only if a compelling indication exists.
examples_of_compelling_OAC_indications_l: Atrial fibrillation (paroxysmal, persistent, or permanent) with CHA2DS2-VASc score ≥1 in men and ≥2 in women
Recent or history of recurrent or unprovoked deep vein thrombosis (DVT) or pulmonary embolism (PE)
clinical_recommendations_and_considerati.antiplatelet_agent_notes: Prasugrel or ticagrelor as part of TAT is not recommended (tested in minority of patients; absence of robust safety/efficacy data).
clinical_recommendations_and_considerati.treatment_intensity: The intensity of OAC should be individualized (text truncated on page).

content.statistical_notes: Reported relative risks, confidence intervals, P values, and absolute event differences were used to present benefit/harm trade-offs (bleeding vs ischemic events).
